Food photography · Creative brief

马来西亚咖哩雞

Malaysian Curry Chicken · Kari Ayam

Prompt

Premium Malaysian restaurant food poster featuring deconstructed layers of 马来西亚咖哩雞 / Malaysian Curry Chicken (Kari Ayam) floating in a vertical stack on pure black background (#000000). Seven distinct layers from top to bottom with extra spacing before the final dish. Layers 1-5 show RAW, UNCOOKED recipe ingredients before cooking; only the bottom finished dish is cooked:

1) Top layer: an airborne cloud of dry, unheated golden-orange Malaysian curry powder, including turmeric, coriander and cumin, with bright red dried chili pieces. Fine spice particles reveal rich color and texture. These are uncooked seasonings, not a fried spice paste.

2) Second layer: fresh, uncooked sliced purple shallots, ivory garlic cloves, fresh ginger slices, pale green bruised lemongrass segments and glossy dark green curry leaves. Show crisp raw textures and clean cut surfaces, without sauteing, charring or browning.

3) Third layer: several fresh RAW bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh and drumstick pieces. Show visibly uncooked pale pink flesh, ivory to pale cream skin and a natural moist sheen. The chicken is plain and unseasoned, with no orange curry coating, golden browning, roasted crust, cooked texture or steam. The chicken is the central protein; no noodles.

4) Fourth layer: chunky freshly peeled RAW potato wedges, with pale ivory to light cream flesh, sharp clean knife-cut edges and a matte starchy surface. A few fresh curry leaves drift around them. The potatoes are unboiled and unfried, without browning, golden crust, orange curry coating or cooked softness. Make the raw potato pieces clearly recognizable and substantial.

5) Fifth layer: a transparent glass bowl filled with opaque creamy WHITE coconut milk, a recipe ingredient before cooking. Show a smooth white liquid surface and realistic glass reflections. No orange curry gravy, spice mixture, red oil droplets or steam in this bowl. The glass bowl floats BELOW the raw potatoes in the vertical stack.

6) Sixth layer: EMPTY SPACE - a larger gap with a few tiny spice particles and subtle steam wisps rising only from the cooked finished dish below. Raw ingredient layers must not emit steam. Preserve the large transition gap and breathing room.

7) Bottom/Final layer (with significantly larger gap above): a complete finished Malaysian Curry Chicken dish in a traditional dark brown ceramic bowl, viewed from the same 45-degree angled perspective as all other layers above. The bowl contains tender cooked bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks and large soft golden potato chunks, generously coated in thick orange-gold coconut curry gravy. Glossy curry leaves and a small visible lemongrass segment complete the dish. The cooked chicken looks succulent and lightly braised, with appetizing textured skin; the potatoes look soft and infused with curry. Subtle steam rises from the warm bowl. The finished bowl is at the same scale and viewing angle as the deconstructed ingredients above. The extra spacing above emphasizes this as the final result, creating a dramatic reveal of the transformation from separated components to a complete dish.

Each layer is separated with gaps revealing textures and details. Layers 1-5 have normal spacing between them. Layer 6 is an intentional empty transition space with double or triple the normal gap distance. Layer 7 (finished dish) sits at the bottom with clear visual separation. Chinese and English bilingual labels in elegant warm cream typography with thin curved arrows pointing to each component. Render these labels verbatim, each once, with the Chinese on the first line and the English directly underneath:
"咖哩香料" / "Curry Spices"
"香料與咖哩葉" / "Aromatics & Curry Leaves"
"生雞肉" / "Raw Chicken"
"生馬鈴薯" / "Raw Potatoes"
"椰奶" / "Coconut Milk"
"成品" / "Finished Dish"

Keep every label legible and fully inside the frame, balanced on the left and right with ample negative space and no overlapping food. Do not label the empty transition gap. Do not add a title, logo, slogan or unrelated text inside the poster.

NO white pedestal, NO platform base. All layers float freely in space against pure black background. Dramatic studio lighting from a 45-degree angle, with rim lighting highlighting chicken skin, potato edges, glossy curry leaves and glass bowl transparency. All layers including the finished bowl share identical lighting, perspective angle and photorealistic quality. Steam rises only from the cooked finished bowl into the empty transition gap. Fine dry spice particles float around the upper raw ingredient layers. Preserve the clear visual progression from uncooked materials to the finished curry. A small star sparkle appears in the bottom right corner near the finished dish. Dark moody aesthetic, luxurious commercial food photography style, ultra-realistic, highly detailed, professional restaurant advertising quality, 9:16 vertical format.
